verdict.why:
I wrote my own classifier (lib.mjs, classify.mjs, marks.mjs, verify.mjs, falsify.mjs, roles.mjs in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-mashiachsonyosef-github-io/c72302ec-11e7-5b6d-a5ab-47bb077585fe/scratchpad/punct/verify/kaikki_wiktionary_hebrew/) and ran it over all 123,558 routes. Run it with: node verify.mjs <jsonl> <census.json> <ghp/reader> <out> [parens|scopes] [reconcile].

The mark census itself matches: 68 marks, and every mark's occurrence and route count agrees with mark-inventory-2026-10-31.json.

(a) Counts. Built from the tests as the declaration words them, 30 of 148 shape rows do not match the draft. The biggest gaps:
- paren.argument_slot: 1,911 against 2,337
- paren.grammar_label: 323 against 436
- comma.before_relative: 66 against 288
- comma.gloss_boundary: 69,974 against 69,591
- comma.pointer: 503 against 302 when "outside parentheses" is read literally, 283 when it means outside every scope

The cause is that many tests end in "..." and none states its precedence. In a second pass I borrowed only the word lists from the draft's script (its constants, used to explain the gaps; every structural rule stayed mine). With those lists, all 145 rows match exactly and so do the division totals (56,309 routes divided, 136,685 pieces, 0 rejoin failures). So the draft's numbers are consistent with its script, but they cannot be reproduced from the declaration as written.

(b) Completeness. The tests as written leave 12 occurrences unexplained: 9 en dashes, 2 gereshes and the 1 '@' at קשיטה. The draft admits only the '@'. About 900 occurrences also pass two tests at once with no precedence stated, the largest being romanization against the apostrophe and hyphen tests (303, 208, 117).

(c) Meanings. Every dividing shape except colon.strongs_list has counterexamples the declaration neither states nor counts. They are listed below.

(d) Comparison with today's global rule (v3). My own v3 path imports sense-split-v1.mjs and copies zone.html's semicolon split and page-citation drop. With the borrowed lists it gives exactly 112,005 same / 1,726 v3 divides, declaration whole / 3,300 declaration divides, v3 whole / 6,495 divided differently / 32 v3 prints nothing. The set of 11,553 disagreeing rows is identical to the draft's file; 186 of them differ only because the draft drops the period at a sentence boundary. The senseSplit-alone figures (108,849 / 1,726 / 5,373 / 7,610) also match. With the lists as written the result is 112,034 / 1,508 / 3,303 / 6,681 / 32.
falsified_meanings: comma.gloss_boundary ('divides one English gloss from the next'): 97 occurrences in 19 route texts where a piece is no gloss. 'i.e.' or 'e.g.' stands alone as a piece (68): השתלט 'to be skilled with, i.e., to have a good command of', בכינים 'crybaby, i.e., a person who…', להקה 'group of animals, e.g.'. Coordinate adjectives split one noun phrase (10): עלמה 'a young, unmarried woman…', גברתן 'a strong, muscular man', אלמים 'A strong, violent person.'. A clause about a named thing becomes a piece (8): כך '…, banned in 1994.', תניא '…, first published in 1797', הינדי '…, now known as Hindustani.', אכזיב '…, located in the territory…'. A KJV list copied without ': -' (7): המלוכה '…: a kingdom, king's, X royal.'. A piece ending '- i.e' (3): בחורה. One name split in two (1): ניצה 'Nice, France'. None of these is covered by the counted exception of 5,326 pieces over 4 words.

semicolon.sense_boundary ('divides one sense group from the next'): 50 occurrences in 8 texts where the next segment is a usage note that the note-opener list misses, so it prints as a reading: מאמירות '; especially figurative.', חרום '; often used attributively', ידידותיים '; especially in extended senses.', כלן '; found almost exclusively…', שום '; found chiefly in negative contexts…', החזיק '; typically used of captives…', טריפים '; found especially in the phrase…'.

semicolon.note_follows ('divides the glosses from a usage note … no reading'): 16 occurrences in 4 texts where the 'also' segment is another sense, so a reading loses its pill: להטן '; also (from the idea of enwrapping) magic' (×13), אפרים '; also the tribe descended from him…', אבדלה '; also, a formula of prayer…', קדר '; also (collectively) Ishmaelite and Bedouin…'.

period.sentence_boundary: 34 occurrences (נערתו and its forms) of 'boy, physically able young man. Also, a servant.'. The period divides correctly, but the opener 'also' makes 'Also, a servant.' a note, though it is a second sense. The same 'also' rule falsifies comma.in_note there.

colon.head_explanation ('divides the head gloss from the explanation that defines it'): 118 occurrences in 18 texts where the explanation is a usage note printed as a reading: עד 'To: used in expressing a range.', איתן 'With: used to indicate togetherness…' (×31), לך 'Of, to, before: indicating the hour…', איני '…: used in expressing non-existence…', בי 'please: used to make a polite request'. In a further 59 occurrences in 10 texts the colon divides inside a segment that opens as a note, which the declaration says is held whole, and the gloss sits on the right: הוא 'Used as a copula: is.', אמן '…: amen', זדה 'Possibilities include: crack, echo'. Also 7 KJV lists (המלוכה) and 3 cases of 'i.e:' (בחורה).

colon.pointer_gloss ('the part after is a reading list'): 36 of 278 occurrences, in 35 texts, where the right side is a further form pointer: רגליך 'Masoretic spelling of רַגְלְךָ: singular form of רֶגֶל…', עלית 'defective spelling of עליית: singular construct state form…'.
colon.gloss_pointer ('the pointer giving its grammar'): 1 case, פרד״ס '…understanding of scripture: פְּשַׁט (p'shát), רֶמֶז…', where the right side is a list of Hebrew terms, not a pointer.

period.before_trailing_note ('a note on the whole line'): 1 case, מטחוי '… (ṭaḥwā). (In the construct state)', which is a grammar label, not a note. Written lowercase, the same label would hold the line instead of dividing it.

The note opener 'it'/'this' catches a gloss: 9 occurrences in 5 texts. זו 'This, this one.' is held whole as a note where v3 divides it. ה־ 'This: the current or adjacent; used…' and הזה 'this: masculine singular definite of זֶה' also become notes.
en_dash.range (non-dividing): 9 spaced apposition dashes were counted as ranges: ארנק 'a wallet – a discreet personal device…', שורוק 'shuruk – a combination of the Hebrew letter…'.

No counterexample found for colon.strongs_list (74): no ':-' without a space, no ';' or sentence '.' inside a KJV list, and both screened non-list hits are real lists. None for the abbreviation list under period.sentence_boundary (0 misses).
corrections: State every word list in full instead of ending it in '...': the note openers (the script adds compare, cf., located, further, as opposed to, possibilities include, '(see'), the clause openers (the script uses 62 words, including also, see, said, known, meaning, including, excluding, except, corresponding), the relative words (adding whom, while, whereas, whether, although, though, unless, therefore, than, so), the labels and one-word labels, the function-word-first list, the end-preposition list and the abbreviations. With the lists as written, 30 shape rows fail to reproduce.

paren.argument_slot: the test must list what the script accepts: someone or something, something or someone, something else, someone else, a thing, an object, people, one, somebody. As worded it gives 1,911, not 2,337.
paren.grammar_label: the script matches (suffix|prefix) conjugation, hence past tense, construct or gerund and construct state, with no form-of-line condition. As worded it gives 323, not 436.
Every 'Hebrew outside parentheses' test (comma.pointer and the colon tests) must say 'outside parentheses and square brackets'. Read literally, comma.pointer is 503, not 302.

State the precedence within each mark: romanization over nested (26), and romanization over the apostrophe and hyphen tests (303 + 208 + 28 + 117 + 23); terminal over ellipsis (2, at לפנה״ס 'C.E..'); range over compound (22); strongs_suffix over bound_suffix (20); nested over argument_slot (19) and mark_display (14); phoneme over spaced alternation (16); per_unit over alternation (7); lead_label over hebrew_note (5); and, for commas, pointer before note.
en_dash.range: the script calls every non-Strong's en dash a range. Add en_dash.apposition (9, non-dividing) or the test leaves them unexplained.
geresh.hebrew: the test should read 'follows a Hebrew letter or point' (2: גירונה, קמבודיה).

comma.gloss_boundary: list the 97 counted exceptions, or add holding tests for them: a lone 'i.e.'/'e.g.' piece, an 'a/an + adjective' first piece, a past-participle clause after a proper name, an X/+ sigil list, and 'City, Country'.

Note detection: add the misses 'especially figurative/in', 'often/typically used', 'found almost/chiefly/exclusively/especially' (50 occurrences). Exempt 'also' followed by an article or '(' when it carries a sense (16 + 34). Exempt a segment that is the gloss 'This'/'It' (9).

colon.head_explanation: an explanation that opens as a note (used, indicating, see …; 118) should take the note role, and a colon inside a note segment (59) should be held or have its roles stated. Otherwise 'the note is held whole' is false.
colon.pointer_gloss: state that the right side can be a further form pointer (36 of 278) and give it the pointer role.
State where the period at a sentence boundary goes. The draft's pieces drop it ('physically able young man') but keep the terminal period, so 186 disagreeing rows differ only there.

The colon and semicolon under_lead_label tests say 'led' only, but the refusal holds closed-label lines too. It is harmless today (0 dividing marks in the 20 closed-label routes), but the test should say 'led or closed'.

pieces_by_role cannot be reproduced from the stated words; the role rules are not written as tests. Mine: head 128,694 / explanation 6,411 / note 676 / pointer 551 / gloss 293 / strongs 60. Draft: 128,791 / 6,351 / 625 / 552 / 292 / 74.

questions: 1. The colon. 5,768 depth-0 colons stand between a head gloss and the explanation that defines it ('A tunnel: an underground or underwater passage'). Reading A (declared): the colon divides, and the head and the explanation are each a reading. Reading B: the explanation defines the head and is not a reading; the head alone is the reading and the explanation prints as the record's note. v3 never divides at ':'. The colon is the cause in 3,135 + 3,170 disagreeing routes.

2. Long pieces in a gloss list. 5,326 pieces of more than 4 words stand beside a dividing comma in 4,981 routes ('cobra, snake of the family Elapidae'; 'to pass, to not fail a test'; also some clauses the opener lists miss, e.g. key כך 'Kach, a far-right ... party ..., banned in 1994'). Reading A (declared): Wiktionary's comma lists equivalents, including a describing one, and divides wherever no clause opener, conjunction, relative, label or etc. follows. Reading B (v3): a piece over 4 words makes the field a sentence; the short pieces are readings and the whole field stands beside them.

3. Pieces that are not readings. Division keeps 625 note pieces and 552 form-pointer pieces ('used in forming questions.'; 'defective spelling of ייצר'). Reading A: each prints as the record's note or pointer, not as a pill. Reading B: each prints as a pill like any other piece. The declaration marks each piece's role and leaves the printing to the owner.

4. Labels over the whole line. 114 routes open with a context label ('(intransitive) to soak, permeate') and 20 close with one after the final period ('To leaven, ferment. (of dough)'). Reading A (declared): ship whole. Reading B: divide them like any line; the label stays on the one piece it was written on. v3 divides 104 of them today.

5. The store's own cut. In 92 rows (M50 66, M69 26) the route is the definition with its lead label removed ('(anatomy) vagina' printed 'vagina'). In 114 other rows (M25 85, M13 19, M50 6, M11 3, M69 1) the lead label stays on the route. Reading A: the store's cut stands, because the label is a topic tag. Reading B: the cut is a derivation, and the route should be the whole definition, as it is in the other rows.

6. Strong's text copied into Wiktionary. 74 routes carry a Strong's ':-' KJV list (238 commas in that list, held whole here). Reading A (declared): hold it whole. Reading B: divide it under the Strong's declaration (wikisource_strongs_explicit_forms), whose convention it is.

7. Unbalanced groups. 32 routes carry a '(' that never closes (truncated notes). Today's card prints nothing for that damaged sense. Reading A (declared): ship each route whole. Reading B: keep today's drop.
